2026-08-26T03:29:51.4915196Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4915563Z 
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4915890Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4916360Z 
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4916762Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4917259Z 
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4918801Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4920492Z >
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4923217Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4925622Z >
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4926417Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4927167Z 
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4927351Z ### How to Use
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4927578Z 
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4928273Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4928973Z 
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4929151Z ```bash
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4929701Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4930411Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4931011Z ```
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4931494Z 
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4931786Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4932323Z ```bash
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4932861Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4933640Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4934484Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4935207Z ```
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4935419Z 
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4936040Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4936896Z ```bash
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4937452Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4938133Z ```
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4938342Z 
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4938791Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4939395Z ```bash
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4939934Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4940787Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4941709Z ```
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4941922Z 
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4942196Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4942627Z 
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4944031Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4945583Z 
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4945757Z ```bash
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4946195Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4947047Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4947872Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4948183Z 
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4948655Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4949647Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4950454Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4950916Z ```
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4951291Z 
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4952042Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4952936Z 
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4953107Z ```bash
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4953775Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4954647Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4955347Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4955789Z 
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4956187Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4956973Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4957518Z ```
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4957715Z 
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4957920Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4958720Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4959676Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4960629Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4961789Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4962845Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4963372Z 
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4963552Z ### Notes
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4963775Z 
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4964377Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4965763Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4967010Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4968246Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4969433Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4970535Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4971678Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-08-26T03:29:51.4972371Z </mcp-clis>
